Question Choices: Select. Look at the shape above. Is it a circle or oval? ~~Circle | Oval~~

right derivation: Compare the vertical and horizontal widths through the center. | Treat those widths as different.
wrong derivation: Compare the vertical and horizontal widths through the center. | Treat those widths as equal.

Question Choices: Select. Does circle has corners? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Corners are pointy parts where two straight lines meet. A circle has no straight lines. Does it has pointy parts?
Solution: A circle has a smooth curved boundary without any corners. Therefore, no, it does not have corners.
right derivation: Trace the boundary looking for sharp meeting points. | Do not count the topmost point as a corner.
wrong derivation: Trace the boundary looking for sharp meeting points. | Count the topmost point as a corner.

Question Choices: Select. Which one is a quadrilateral?: ~~Circle | Square | Triangle~~

Solution: Count the straight sides: the square has 4, the triangle has 3 and the circle has 0. Choose Square.
right derivation: A quadrilateral needs four straight sides. | Read the triangle as having 3 sides.
wrong derivation: A quadrilateral needs four straight sides. | Read the triangle as having 4 sides.

Hints: This shape has only 1 pair of "never crossing" lines. It is a special 4-sided shape that is not a square or a rectangle or a diamond.
Solution: The pictured quadrilateral has one pair of parallel sides: the top and bottom. It is a trapezoid.
right derivation: Check opposite sides and corner angles. | Count 1 parallel pairs and 0 right angles.

right derivation: Check equal side lengths and right angles separately. | Read the pictured shape as having 0 right angles.

Question Choices: Select. Which one has more sides, triangle or rectangle? ~~Triangle | Rectangle~~
Hints: Draw each shape and count the sides| triangle has 3 sides, rectangle has 4 sides
Solution: The rectangle has 4 sides and the triangle has 3. Since 4 is greater than 3, the rectangle has more sides.
right derivation: Compare the number of straight sides. | Read the triangle as having 3 sides.
wrong derivation: Compare the number of straight sides. | Read the triangle as having 5 sides.

Question Choices: Select. Is a square also a rectangle? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: A rectangle needs 4 sides and 4 right angles. A square has those too plus all sides equal. So is a square a special kind of rectangle?
Solution: A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles. A square has four right angles, so every square is a rectangle.
right derivation: A rectangle requires four right angles. | Count 4 right angles in the square.
wrong derivation: A rectangle requires four right angles. | Count 2 right angles in the square.

Question Choices: Select. Is a square also a rhombus? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: All shapes with 4 equal sides are rhombus| square is a special rhombus
Solution: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with four equal sides. A square has four equal sides, so every square is a rhombus.
right derivation: A rhombus requires all four sides to be equal. | Count 4 equal-length sides in the square.
wrong derivation: A rhombus requires all four sides to be equal. | Count 2 equal-length sides in the square.
